title: Separate era intercepts remove 91% of the 1871-2010 mean SST feedback gap in nine controlled model pairs
abstract: We separate era-level and within-era contributions to the AMIP-minus-HadISST1 radiation-on-temperature slope gap in nine controlled atmosphere-model pairs. With separate intercepts before 1982 and from 1982, the 1871-2010 mean gap changes from -0.283 to -0.025 W m-2 K-1. The level contribution is -0.258, or 91% of the sample mean gap, and is negative in all nine pairs. A synchronous five-year block bootstrap gives limits of -0.373 to -0.174 for this contribution; the remaining gap has limits of -0.120 to +0.095. Removing 1982 or 1981-1983 retains level shares of 81% and 85%. Yet 1983-2010 slopes still differ in eight of nine pairs, with mean gap -0.379. This limits a general claim that one lasting step explains all dataset dependence. The method is an exact covariance audit, not an SST correction. Era intercepts remove real slow climate responses as well as possible errors. Annual global ensemble means cannot identify which SST dataset is correct or prove that the source splice caused the full era contrast.
